title: The end of a plate: a summary, three equal actions, a question only where it is needed
why: Coach Milan 18 November 19:51: Ate it shows as a blue chip; is it a button or a status? 20 November 16:05: Ate it is clicked and nothing changed. 16:08: the flow with the question and the chips is not UX; rethink the flow and the design. 16:13: yes to the rethought flow. 18:57 to 19:21: the situations; a fixed set of actions, never a button that turns into a status; no scroll on a tap, ask where it happens; a summary of the plate before What do you do with it?; draw it.

opportunity.from: Coach Milan's own look at the B151 board and the app, 18 and 20 November 2026.
opportunity.job: At the end of a plate, log what I ate in one tap, and later see at a glance that the meal is eaten.
opportunity.kind: Too many steps, and did not understand it: the meal is chosen in two places, and the tap on Ate it changes nothing you can see.
opportunity.why_now: Every plate ends here, so every meal logged goes through it.

problem: The meal is chosen in two places. At the top, Meal and day says No meal selected, with its pencil. At the end, a question, What do you do with it?, and three chips that look alike; Ate it opens a second calendar to choose the meal again. In the first drawing Ate it stayed white, so the tap changed nothing on it. And a meal I ate, opened again, says nothing about being eaten.
story: When my plate is ready, I want to say I ate it in one tap for the meal I am at, so that it counts without choosing the meal twice.
now: The top line says No meal selected. The end asks What do you do with it? with three chips; Ate it turns blue and opens a calendar; a tap on a meal logs it and Today opens. The meal opened again shows no status.
proposed: The meal is set at the top (the pencil). At the end, before What do you do with it?, a summary of the plate: its name, its numbers, and the meal it is for, or No meal selected. Then Save it, Plan it and Ate it: three equal white actions that never change their look. With a meal set, a tap acts at once. With none, a short question opens right under the tapped button, joined to it: Which meal was it? with today's meals, the one the time suggests marked; one tap logs it and the summary and the top line show the same meal. No scrolling on a tap. Ate it logs and Today opens, as now; the meal opened again shows Ate it blue with a tick on its left.
looked_at: A guess shown at the top: not chosen, the meal stays set only by you (DT308.1). A main, filled button that follows the meal: not chosen, a button that changes its look by the state is a status. Scrolling up to the top line on a tap: not chosen, by the time it gets there the person has lost what it was about. An open look for Ate it with a second calendar: not chosen, two places for one choice.
decision: Coach Milan 20 November 19:21: draw it, to see whether it makes sense. Waits for his look.

ac.title: A summary before the question
ac.text: Given skyr, oats and a banana on the Plate, when I reach the end of the plate, then above What do you do with it? it says Skyr, Oats & Banana, 563 kcal, 39 g protein, PD 7.0, and the meal it is for or No meal selected

ac.title: Three equal actions
ac.text: Given the end of the plate, when I look at it, then Save it, Plan it and Ate it are white buttons of one look, whatever meal is set, and none of them turns into a status

ac.title: A set meal, at once
ac.text: Given I set Dinner with the pencil, when I tap Ate it, then the plate is logged as today's Dinner and Today opens, with no question

ac.title: No meal, asked right there
ac.text: Given no meal is set, when I tap Ate it, then Which meal was it? opens right under it with today's meals, Dinner marked as the time suggests, and the page does not scroll

ac.title: One tap logs
ac.text: Given the question is open, when I tap Dinner, then the plate is logged as today's Dinner and Today opens

ac.title: The second tap closes
ac.text: Given the question is open, when I tap Ate it again, then the question closes and nothing is logged

ac.title: Plan it the same way
ac.text: Given no meal is set, when I tap Plan it, then For which meal? opens right under it with the meals still ahead today and Another day

ac.title: An eaten meal says Ate it
ac.text: Given I ate it as Dinner, when I open it again from Today, the Plan or a recipe's log, then Ate it is blue with a small tick on its left, before Dinner, 18:00, and a tap on it does nothing

unchanged: What Save it does: the plate into My recipes.
Edit mode behind the pencil: the meals, the X that closes it, No meal selected.
What Ate it logs, and where it takes you: Today, or the Plan for another day.
Today's meal line: Eaten, by the plan; Undo; Change or delete.
A plate from a photo: the read and Did you eat it?, as now.
A plate from earlier: it asks as it does (DT314).
checks: Full: the end of the plate is shared by many flows (a plate, a recipe, a plate from earlier, Prepare it), so all walkthroughs, about 45 minutes, plus the unit tests, the build and a new walkthrough for AC1 to AC8. The walkthroughs that tap the old chips and the calendar under Ate it change with this approved board. New words, so the German sweep too.

boardTitle: B151: the end of a plate. A summary, three equal actions, and a question only where it is needed
details: The pictures are the real app on Sunday 15 November 2026, 18:00, from one scratch build of 0.3.170, not committed. The new words are English drafts: No meal selected: nothing counts yet. Which meal was it? Today, 18:00. Marked: the meal the time suggests. One tap logs it.
Plan it's question (AC7) is not drawn: it works as Ate it's, with the meals ahead and Another day.
Save it stays a white button; after it, a line under the buttons says Saved in My recipes, with the name.
